newsitem.title: USA: U.S. airlines cut fares to compete with American.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlines cut fares to compete with American.

text.p: Four major U.S. air carriers slashed fares on selected routes this weekend after American Airlines lowered ticket prices on Saturday to win back customers scared away by the threat of pilots' strike.
Continental Airlines, United Airlines, Northwest Airlines and America West said they were now offering fares competitive with American's prices.
Delta Air Lines and USAir said they had not yet made a decision on cutting prices.
American and its commuter carrier, American Eagle, announced a fare sale on Saturday with discounts of up to 50 percent on regular excursion fares.

The airline cut the fares only hours after President Bill Clinton stepped in to end a pilots' strike. He acted minutes after union leaders called a strike by American's 9,300 pilots at 12:01 a.m. Saturday (0501 GMT on Saturday).
The short-lived strike followed five days of intense negotiations with management that failed to bring agreement on a new four-year labour contract.
On Sunday, Continental spokeswoman Sarah Anthony said: "We are competitive with what American initiated in all the markets where they have dropped their fares."
Anthony said Continental lowered its fares on Saturday as soon as it learned of the American reductions. Its sale is to end on March 3, it said.

American's sales prices would apply to tickets bought between now and March 3 and no advance purchase was needed, the airline said. It was also offering double air miles and complimentary upgrades for its frequent fliers.
United Airlines said it was matching American's cuts on both international and domestic flights.

American's discounts averaged 50 percent on excursion fares in all American and American Eagle markets in Canada and the United States, including Hawaii, for travel through March 14, with discounts of about 45 percent for travel until May 31. For European flights, fares would be cut up to 50 percent until May 31, the airline said.
American also promised discounts of 25 to 30 percent on weekday and weekend excursion fares to the Caribbean and the Bahamas until May 31.
Northwest said it was offering discounts of up to 50 percent off in select markets in wake of the American reductions. "We'll come pretty close to matching their fares," a spokeswoman said.

America West spokesman Gus Whitcomb said: "We have matched American's fares in select markets, but on off-peak and night flights, our fares are lower." He said off-peak was Tuesday, Wednesday and Saturday, while special night flight rates were offered daily. They announced cuts effective on Sunday.
A USAir spokesman said the airline was studying the issue but had not taken any action yet.
Trans World Airlines on Saturday matched American's new fares but said it had not decided whether to match the frequent flier mile offer.
